acceptance_criteria.given: a scratch project, a Haiku agent whose worktree exists, then a file committed to master
acceptance_criteria.how_to_check: py -3.11 scripts/drive/d1015_f607_worktree_catch_up.py <project> (written first: the agent could not find the file on HEAD)
acceptance_criteria.then: the worktree contains master's commit and the reply quotes the file
acceptance_criteria.when: the agent's next turn reads the file

acceptance_criteria.then: fast-forwarded, merged, untouched, untouched with the merge aborted
acceptance_criteria.when: the worktree is behind, diverged, dirty, or conflicting

design: Tier 1. No migration. D1. The target is the same integration base a task branch is cut from (`task_workspace.integration_base`), so an agent and its tasks see one main. D2. Non-blocking, unlike the task catch-up (which refuses): an agent's own checkout is not a deliverable, and refusing its mail over a conflict would be an outage; the conflict is logged. D3. In `worktrees.resolve_turn_workspace`, on the agent arm only.

checked: task catch-up exists for prerequisites only (worktrees._catch_up_prerequisites)
drive on HEAD: the file committed after the worktree was cut is not seen

problem: `worktrees.ensure_worktree` cuts an agent's branch once and nothing moves it afterwards, while task checkouts catch up with their approved prerequisites (F158). A reconcile turn ran on a worktree lacking landed code and recorded three false 'missing' gaps (2026-10-15 sweep G4); a turn could not find a file committed to master after its worktree was cut (F602's drive; re-driven on HEAD: 'RELEASE.txt does not exist in my workspace').

requirements.rationale: Reconcile, exploration and mail turns read the agent's checkout as the project's code.
requirements.statement: Before an untasked turn starts in a writing agent's own worktree, the worktree MUST contain the commit of the project's integration base (Project.main_branch when set and resolving, else the project checkout's HEAD): fast-forwarded when it has no commits of its own, merged when it has and is clean.

requirements.rationale: An agent's own uncommitted work must not be lost to a catch-up.
requirements.statement: A worktree with uncommitted changes, or whose merge conflicts, MUST be left exactly as it was (the merge aborted) and the turn MUST still run.
Task checkouts, review checkouts and read-only agents MUST be unaffected.

in_scope: writing agents' own worktrees on untasked turns
non_goals: telling the agent its checkout is behind when catch-up was declined

summary: Before an untasked turn runs in a writing agent's own worktree, the worktree takes in what the project's integration base has that it lacks: fast-forward, or a merge when it carries commits of its own; uncommitted work or a conflict leaves it untouched and the turn runs as before (F607, also seen live in F602's drive).
title: An agent's own checkout is brought up to main before its turn
